lede: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.33% to 50,182.95 at the 16:00 New York close on November 25, after recovering from a loss of more than 1,100 points, CNBC reported. The S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,182.78 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62% to 23,585.80. A selloff in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks led by Nvidia drove the declines, and Oracle fell more than 5%, according to CNBC. The Bureau of Economic Analysis says the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose 3.8% in the year to October and 3.3% excluding food and energy, and that third-quarter growth was revised up to a 4.3% annual rate.

items.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average closes up 0.33% after recovering a 1,100-point loss
facts: At the 16:00 New York close on November 25, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.33% to 50,182.95 and the S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,182.78, CNBC reported.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62% to 23,585.80 at the close, after falling about 4.6% at its low of the session, according to CNBC.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average had been down more than 1,100 points during the session before it closed higher, CNBC reported.
items.why: Technology shares led the swings. US markets are closed on Thursday, November 26, for Thanksgiving, so this was the last full session before the holiday.

items.title: Oracle falls more than 5% as the tech selloff led by Nvidia resumes
facts: Oracle shares fell more than 5% on November 25 during a broad selloff in technology stocks, CNBC reported.
Nvidia led the decline after its earlier rally faded and worries about artificial intelligence (AI) returned, according to CNBC.
Technology shares closed well above their lows of the session, and Anthropic struggled to climb back above its initial public offering (IPO) price, CNBC reported.
items.why: Oracle's fall adds to pressure on companies spending heavily on AI data centers, and it weighed on the Nasdaq Composite and on software stocks.

items.title: Dell posts record $54.9 billion revenue, sees $202 billion for the year
facts: Dell Technologies reported record revenue of $54.9 billion for its fiscal third quarter in a release filed on November 24.
Artificial intelligence (AI) orders reached $60.2 billion in the quarter, leaving a record AI backlog of $132.3 billion at quarter end.
Dell now expects fiscal 2027 revenue of about $202.0 billion, a 78% increase from the prior year.
items.why: The AI backlog shows server demand, and it bears on AI chip suppliers and on server makers such as Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Super Micro Computer.

items.title: Medtronic revenue rises 4.5% to $9.36 billion; full-year outlook held
facts: Medtronic reported fiscal second-quarter revenue of $9.364 billion on November 24, up 4.5% as reported and 6.5% on an organic basis.

Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) came in at $1.34. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) (generally accepted accounting principles) EPS was $2.20, including a $2.0 billion gain from the MiniMed separation.
Medtronic kept its fiscal 2027 targets of 7.25% to 7.75% organic revenue growth and adjusted EPS of $5.94 to $6.00. Cardiac ablation sales grew 58%.
items.why: Cardiac ablation growth affects medical-device rivals Boston Scientific, Abbott and Johnson & Johnson. An unchanged outlook steadies health-care equipment shares.

items.title: Workday revenue grows 11.2% to $2.705 billion, buys back $750 million of stock
facts: Workday reported total revenue of $2.705 billion for the quarter ended October 31, up 11.2%. Subscription revenue rose 12.8% to $2.532 billion.

Non-GAAP (excluding items under generally accepted accounting principles) earnings per share were $2.82. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) operating income of $329 million included $51 million of restructuring charges.
The 12-month subscription revenue backlog rose 12.3% to $9.216 billion. Workday bought back about 3.8 million shares for $750 million.
items.why: Backlog growth shows demand for enterprise software, which bears on application-software shares weighing artificial intelligence risk, such as Salesforce and ServiceNow.

items.title: HP fourth-quarter revenue rises 9.3% to $16.0 billion; adjusted earnings per share tops outlook
facts: HP Inc. reported fourth-quarter net revenue of $16.0 billion on November 24, up 9.3% from a year earlier and up 8.6% in constant currency.
Non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share (EPS) were $0.83, above HP's outlook of $0.69 to $0.79. The figure includes about $0.15 from tariff refunds; the year-earlier figure was $0.93.
Adjusted EPS for fiscal 2026 was $3.33, up from $3.12. The company cited rising memory and storage costs as a pressure.
items.why: Rising memory chip costs squeeze margins at personal computer and printer makers, including Dell, and support pricing for memory suppliers such as Micron.

items.title: Beige Book finds growth in 8 of 12 Federal Reserve districts
facts: Eight of the 12 Federal Reserve districts reported slight to moderate growth and four reported no change, the Beige Book released on November 25 said.
Employment rose slightly on balance; prices rose moderately, and input costs grew faster than selling prices.
The information was collected on or before November 16, ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on December 8-9.
items.why: Persistent cost pressures and steady hiring support the case for tighter policy, which bears on short-dated Treasury yields before the December 9 decision.

items.title: Cards overtake cash in euro area shops for first time, European Central Bank study finds
facts: Cards were used in 45% of point-of-sale transactions in the euro area in 2026 and cash in 44%, the European Central Bank (ECB) said on November 25.
82% of consumers said it is important to have the option to pay digitally, and 62% valued the option to pay with cash.
Cash was accepted at 93% of points of sale, down from 95% in 2024, according to the survey of 51,551 respondents.
items.why: The shift toward cards supports transaction volumes for card networks and payment processors and feeds into the ECB's digital euro debate.

items.title: Sweden signs agreement to settle krona payments on the Eurosystem's T2 platform
facts: The European Central Bank and Sveriges Riksbank signed an agreement on November 25 for Sweden to settle large-value Swedish krona payments in T2.
Migration from Sweden's national settlement platform is targeted for February 2030.
The Swedish krona would be the second non-euro currency on T2, after the Danish krone.
items.why: Moving krona settlement onto Eurosystem infrastructure changes how Swedish banks handle large-value payments and their liquidity, with no change to monetary policy.

items.title: US personal consumption expenditures prices rise 0.3% in October, up 3.8% from a year earlier
facts: The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose 0.3% in October from September and 3.8% from October 2025, the Bureau of Economic Analysis said on November 25.
Excluding food and energy, the PCE price index also rose 0.3% on the month and 3.3% from a year earlier.
Disposable personal income rose 0.8% and consumer spending rose 0.3%; the personal saving rate rose to 4.1% from 3.6% in September.
items.why: Core inflation at 3.3%, well above the Federal Reserve's 2% goal, bears on Treasury yields and the Fed's December 8-9 rate decision.

items.title: US third-quarter growth is revised up to a 4.3% annual rate
facts: Real gross domestic product (GDP) grew at a 4.3% annual rate in the third quarter of 2026, the Bureau of Economic Analysis said in its second estimate on November 25.
The advance estimate had put third-quarter growth at 3.4%; the upgrade mainly reflects higher estimates of investment and consumer spending.
The Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes its third estimate of third-quarter GDP on December 23.
items.why: Faster growth alongside 3.8% personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation lowers the case for rate cuts and supports short-dated Treasury yields and the dollar.

items.title: US jobless claims fall 13,000 to 189,000
facts: Initial claims for state unemployment benefits fell by 13,000 to a seasonally adjusted 189,000 in the week ended November 21, the Labor Department said on November 25.
The prior week's level was revised to 202,000; the report came out a day early because of the Thanksgiving holiday.
Continuing claims fell by 95,000 to 1,697,000 in the week ended November 14, putting the insured unemployment rate at 1.1%.
items.why: Layoffs remain very low, a tight labor market that supports consumer stocks and weakens the case for lower interest rates.

items.title: US durable goods orders rise 0.2% in October to $346.7 billion
facts: New orders for manufactured durable goods rose 0.2% to $346.7 billion in October, the Census Bureau said in its advance report on November 25.
Shipments rose 0.5% to $338.6 billion, and unfilled orders rose 0.8% to $1,637.2 billion.
Orders for nondefense capital goods excluding aircraft, a proxy for business investment, rose 1.2%.
items.why: Rising core capital goods orders point to firm equipment spending, which supports industrial and machinery shares and fourth-quarter growth estimates.

items.title: US consumer confidence jumps to 103.3 in November, highest since January 2025
facts: The Conference Board's consumer confidence index rose 11.4 points to 103.3 in November from 91.9 in October, it said on November 24.
The Present Situation Index rose 13.7 points to 132.8, and the Expectations Index rose 9.9 points to 83.6.
Respondents gave a better view of current and future labor market conditions; the preliminary results had a cutoff date of November 17.
items.why: Stronger confidence going into the holiday season supports retail and consumer discretionary shares and estimates of fourth-quarter spending.
